version = { attr = "logsift.__version__" }

"""Apache/nginx Common Log Format, and Combined, which is a superset.

SPEC 11.1::

    %h %l %u %t "%r" %>s %b [ "%{Referer}i" "%{User-agent}i" ]

The parser is a module-level instance (``PARSER``), so the compiled regex and
the month table are built once per process, as SPEC 4.1 requires of anything
published to the entry point group.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections.abc import Sequence
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Final

from logsift.plugin import API_VERSION
from logsift.record import ParseResult
from logsift.timeparse import parse_iso8601

# A quoted field ends at the first unescaped quote. Apache escapes an embedded
# quote as \" and a backslash as \\, so the alternation must consume an
# escape pair whole or `"GET /a\"b"` would end early at the inner quote.
_QUOTED: Final = r'(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*'

_LINE_RE: Final = re.compile(
    r"(?P<ip>\S+) (?P<ident>\S+) (?P<user>\S+) "
    r"\[(?P<time>[^\]]*)\] "
    rf'"(?P<request>{_QUOTED})" '
    r"(?P<status>[0-9]{3}) (?P<bytes>[0-9]+|-)"
    rf'(?: "(?P<referer>{_QUOTED})" "(?P<user_agent>{_QUOTED})")?'
)

# Fixed English table, never strptime("%b"): %b reads LC_TIME, so a server
# running under a German locale would stop parsing its own logs (SPEC 11.1).
_MONTHS: Final = {
    "Jan": 1,
    "Feb": 2,
    "Mar": 3,
    "Apr": 4,
    "May": 5,
    "Jun": 6,
    "Jul": 7,
    "Aug": 8,
    "Sep": 9,
    "Oct": 10,
    "Nov": 11,
    "Dec": 12,
}

_TIME_RE: Final = re.compile(
    r"(?P<day>[0-9]{2})/(?P<month>[A-Za-z]{3})/(?P<year>[0-9]{4})"
    r":(?P<clock>[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}) (?P<offset>[+-][0-9]{4})"
)

_ESCAPE_RE: Final = re.compile(r"\\(.)")

# `-` in any of these positions is Apache for "nothing was recorded". SPEC 1
# forbids turning that into a fact, so it becomes None rather than "-" or 0.
_ABSENT: Final = "-"


def _unescape(text: str) -> str:
    """Undo Apache's ``\\"`` and ``\\\\`` escaping inside a quoted field."""
    return _ESCAPE_RE.sub(r"\1", text)


def _optional(value: str) -> str | None:
    return None if value == _ABSENT else value


def _parse_time(text: str) -> datetime | None:
    """Read ``10/Oct/2000:13:55:36 -0700`` into an aware datetime.

    The month is resolved through the English table and the rest is handed to
    ``parse_iso8601``, which already owns calendar validation and the offset
    range check. Rewriting either here would be a second copy that drifts.
    """
    match = _TIME_RE.fullmatch(text)
    if match is None:
        return None
    month = _MONTHS.get(match["month"])
    if month is None:
        return None
    iso = (
        f"{match['year']}-{month:02d}-{match['day']}T{match['clock']}{match['offset']}"
    )
    return parse_iso8601(iso)


def _split_request(request: str) -> tuple[str | None, str | None, str | None]:
    """Split ``GET /path HTTP/1.1`` into method, path, and protocol.

    A path may legally contain a space, so the protocol is recognized by its
    ``HTTP/`` prefix at the end rather than by counting words. A request line
    that does not split (nginx logs a bare ``-`` for a request it never read)
    yields three ``None``s; the raw text still survives as ``message``.
    """
    parts = request.split(" ")
    if len(parts) >= 3 and parts[-1].startswith("HTTP/"):
        return parts[0], " ".join(parts[1:-1]), parts[-1]
    if len(parts) == 2:
        return parts[0], parts[1], None
    return None, None, None


class CommonLogParser:
    """The ``clf`` parser. Stateless, so one instance serves every source."""

    api_version: int = API_VERSION
    name: str = "clf"
    priority: int = 50
    columns: Sequence[str] = ("ts", "ip", "method", "path", "status", "bytes")

    def can_parse(self, sample: Sequence[str]) -> bool:
        """True when a majority of the sample is a well-formed CLF line."""
        considered = 0
        matched = 0
        for line in sample:
            if not line.strip():
                continue
            considered += 1
            if self.parse(line) is not None:
                matched += 1
        return considered > 0 and matched * 2 > considered

    def parse(self, line: str) -> ParseResult | None:
        match = _LINE_RE.fullmatch(line)
        if match is None:
            return None
        ts = _parse_time(match["time"])
        if ts is None:
            # The shape was right and the timestamp was not. Declining the
            # line keeps SPEC 1's "never invent a fact": a record with the
            # fields but no ts would read as a log that carries no time.
            return None

        request = _unescape(match["request"])
        method, path, protocol = _split_request(request)
        fields: dict[str, object] = {
            "ip": match["ip"],
            "ident": _optional(match["ident"]),
            "user": _optional(match["user"]),
            "method": method,
            "path": path,
            "protocol": protocol,
            "status": int(match["status"]),
            "bytes": None if match["bytes"] == _ABSENT else int(match["bytes"]),
        }
        if match["referer"] is not None:
            fields["referer"] = _optional(_unescape(match["referer"]))
            fields["user_agent"] = _optional(_unescape(match["user_agent"]))

        # level stays None: CLF has no severity, and a status code is not one.
        return ParseResult(ts=ts, level=None, message=request, fields=fields)


PARSER: Final = CommonLogParser()

"""The record model of SPEC section 3.

A parser produces a :class:`ParseResult`; the core turns it into a
:class:`Record`, filling in the provenance a plugin must not be able to forge.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import enum
from collections.abc import Mapping
from datetime import datetime
from types import MappingProxyType
from typing import NamedTuple


class Level(enum.IntEnum):
    """Severity, ordered. The core owns the ordering; parsers translate to it."""

    TRACE = 10
    DEBUG = 20
    INFO = 30
    WARN = 40
    ERROR = 50
    FATAL = 60


class ParseResult(NamedTuple):
    """What a parser returns for one line. Any of the three may be ``None``."""

    ts: datetime | None
    level: Level | None
    message: str | None
    fields: Mapping[str, object]


_NO_FIELDS: Mapping[str, object] = MappingProxyType({})


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Record:
    """One log line, parsed or not.

    ``fields`` is copied and wrapped in a ``MappingProxyType`` at construction,
    so a parser that keeps a reference to the mapping it handed over cannot
    mutate a record afterwards. That also makes a record unhashable, which is
    fine: records stream, they are never keys.
    """

    raw: str
    source: str
    lineno: int
    ts: datetime | None
    level: Level | None
    message: str | None
    fields: Mapping[str, object]
    parse_error: bool
    parse_error_reason: str | None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        object.__setattr__(self, "fields", MappingProxyType(dict(self.fields)))

    @classmethod
    def parse_error_record(
        cls, *, raw: str, source: str, lineno: int, reason: str
    ) -> Record:
        """A record for a line no parser understood (SPEC sections 3 and 4.3).

        The one place that builds the "nothing was parsed" shape, so the
        invariant cannot drift between the call sites in the pipeline.
        """
        return cls(
            raw=raw,
            source=source,
            lineno=lineno,
            ts=None,
            level=None,
            message=None,
            fields=_NO_FIELDS,
            parse_error=True,
            parse_error_reason=reason,
        )

"""ISO 8601 reading and time zone helpers (SPEC sections 2.1 and 7).

``datetime.fromisoformat`` on Python 3.10 refuses a trailing ``Z`` and any
fractional-second length other than 3 or 6 digits, so the core owns its own
reader. It is used by the filter language, by the pipeline, and by any parser
that wants it.

Everything here is pure. The one-time "assuming timezone X" diagnostic of
SPEC 7 is emitted by ``pipeline``, which owns diagnostics; keeping it out of
this module is what lets these functions be property-tested.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone, tzinfo
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo, ZoneInfoNotFoundError

# Extended format only, and ASCII digits only: `\d` also matches Arabic-Indic
# and other Unicode digits, which `int()` would happily accept.
_DATE = r"(?P<year>[0-9]{4})-(?P<month>[0-9]{2})-(?P<day>[0-9]{2})"
_TIME = (
    r"(?P<hour>[0-9]{2}):(?P<minute>[0-9]{2})"
    r"(?::(?P<second>[0-9]{2})(?:\.(?P<fraction>[0-9]{1,9}))?)?"
)
_OFFSET = r"(?P<offset>[Zz]|[+-][0-9]{2}(?::?[0-9]{2})?)"
# An offset needs a time to attach to, so the whole tail is one optional group.
_ISO_RE = re.compile(rf"{_DATE}(?:[Tt ]{_TIME}{_OFFSET}?)?")

_MICROSECOND_DIGITS = 6


class UnknownZone(Exception):
    """``--assume-tz`` or ``--tz`` named an unusable zone; the CLI exits 2."""


def parse_iso8601(text: str) -> datetime | None:
    """Read an ISO 8601 timestamp, or return ``None``. Never raises.

    Accepted::

        YYYY-MM-DD[(T|t|space)HH:MM[:SS[.f{1,9}]][offset]]

    where *offset* is ``Z``, ``z``, ``+HH:MM``, ``+HHMM``, or ``+HH`` (and the
    ``-`` forms). A bare date is midnight, matching ``fromisoformat``. Without
    an offset the result is **naive**; SPEC 7 leaves it to the core to decide
    what zone that means.

    Fractional digits past the sixth are truncated rather than rounded,
    because a ``datetime`` stores microseconds and logsift will not invent
    precision it cannot hold. Deliberately outside the grammar: basic format
    (``20260901T100000Z``), ``24:00`` end-of-day, leap second ``:60``, comma
    fractions, offsets with seconds, and surrounding whitespace. Each of those
    returns ``None``, which for a parser means the raw string is kept instead.
    """
    match = _ISO_RE.fullmatch(text)
    if match is None:
        return None

    offset = match["offset"]
    if offset is None:
        zone = None
    else:
        zone = _offset_zone(offset)
        if zone is None:
            return None

    fraction = match["fraction"]
    microsecond = (
        int(fraction.ljust(_MICROSECOND_DIGITS, "0")[:_MICROSECOND_DIGITS])
        if fraction is not None
        else 0
    )

    try:
        return datetime(
            int(match["year"]),
            int(match["month"]),
            int(match["day"]),
            int(match["hour"] or 0),
            int(match["minute"] or 0),
            int(match["second"] or 0),
            microsecond,
            tzinfo=zone,
        )
    except ValueError:
        # Month 13, 30 February, hour 24, a leap second: the shape was right
        # and the values were not.
        return None


def _offset_zone(text: str) -> timezone | None:
    """Turn a matched offset into a fixed zone, or ``None`` if out of range."""
    if text in ("Z", "z"):
        return timezone.utc
    digits = text[1:].replace(":", "")
    hours = int(digits[:2])
    minutes = int(digits[2:]) if digits[2:] else 0
    if hours > 23 or minutes > 59:
        return None
    delta = timedelta(hours=hours, minutes=minutes)
    return timezone(-delta if text[0] == "-" else delta)


def is_naive(dt: datetime) -> bool:
    """Whether ``dt`` carries no usable offset.

    A ``tzinfo`` whose ``utcoffset()`` returns ``None`` is naive in every way
    that matters: ``astimezone`` cannot convert it. One implementation, so the
    subtlety is not re-derived at each call site.
    """
    return dt.tzinfo is None or dt.tzinfo.utcoffset(dt) is None


def to_utc(dt: datetime, assume_tz: tzinfo) -> datetime | None:
    """Normalize to UTC, localizing a naive ``dt`` with ``assume_tz`` (SPEC 7).

    An aware ``dt`` is converted and ``assume_tz`` is ignored. Localization
    keeps ``dt.fold``, which defaults to 0, so an ambiguous local time (the
    repeated hour when DST ends) reads as the *first* of the two and a
    nonexistent one (the skipped hour when DST starts) takes the offset in
    force before the gap. That is a documented choice, not a guess: logsift
    has nothing in the log to disambiguate with.

    ``None`` means the shifted timestamp falls outside the ``datetime``
    domain, which happens within a day of year 1 and year 9999 -- and
    ``9999-12-31`` is a popular "never expires" sentinel. The caller has no
    timestamp to work with in that case, but the line is still a line, so this
    is a value rather than an exception.
    """
    if is_naive(dt):
        dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=assume_tz)
    try:
        return dt.astimezone(timezone.utc)
    except OverflowError:
        return None


def resolve_zone(name: str) -> ZoneInfo:
    """Look up an IANA zone name for ``--assume-tz`` / ``--tz``.

    Raises :class:`UnknownZone` for a name the system's tzdata does not
    provide, and for one ``zoneinfo`` rejects outright (absolute or traversing
    paths). A genuine I/O failure reading tzdata is left to propagate: that is
    a broken system, not a bad zone name.
    """
    try:
        return ZoneInfo(name)
    except (ZoneInfoNotFoundError, ValueError) as exc:
        raise UnknownZone(f"unknown timezone {name!r}: {exc}") from exc


def local_zone() -> tzinfo:
    """The system local zone, the default for ``--assume-tz`` (SPEC 7).

    This is a *fixed offset* taken from the current moment, because the
    standard library cannot name the local IANA zone and ``zoneinfo`` cannot
    reverse-lookup one from an offset. A log written on the other side of a
    DST transition is therefore localized with today's offset; pass
    ``--assume-tz`` to get a zone that knows its own history. The stderr line
    that reports the assumption is what keeps this visible.
    """
    zone = datetime.now().astimezone().tzinfo
    if zone is None:  # pragma: no cover - astimezone() is always aware
        return timezone.utc
    return zone


def zone_label(zone: tzinfo) -> str:
    """A name for ``zone`` to print in a diagnostic.

    An IANA key when there is one, otherwise the abbreviation the zone reports
    for now (``PKT``), which is what :func:`local_zone` can offer.
    """
    if isinstance(zone, ZoneInfo):
        return zone.key
    return zone.tzname(datetime.now()) or str(zone)

1	"""The parser plugin contract of SPEC section 4.
2	
3	Parsers reach the core only through the ``logsift.parsers`` entry point group,
4	including logsift's own. Nothing here imports a specific parser.
5	"""
6	
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	import re
10	import sys
11	from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Sequence
12	from dataclasses import dataclass
13	from importlib.metadata import EntryPoint, entry_points
14	from typing import Protocol, cast, runtime_checkable
15	
16	from logsift.record import ParseResult
17	
18	API_VERSION = 1
19	ENTRY_POINT_GROUP = "logsift.parsers"
20	
21	_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9_-]+")
22	_REQUIRED_ATTRS = ("api_version", "name", "priority", "columns", "can_parse", "parse")
23	
24	WarnFn = Callable[[str], None]
25	
26	
27	@runtime_checkable
28	class Parser(Protocol):
29	    """What an entry point must resolve to. Structural, never inherited."""
30	
31	    api_version: int
32	    name: str
33	    priority: int
34	    columns: Sequence[str]
35	
36	    def can_parse(self, sample: Sequence[str]) -> bool: ...
37	
38	    def parse(self, line: str) -> ParseResult | None: ...
39	
40	
41	class PluginError(Exception):
42	    """A parser could not be selected. The CLI turns this into exit code 2."""
43	
44	
45	class UnknownParser(PluginError):
46	    """``--parser`` named something no installed distribution provides."""
47	
48	
49	class AmbiguousParser(PluginError):
50	    """``--parser NAME`` matched more than one distribution (SPEC 4.4)."""
51	
52	
53	def warn_stderr(message: str) -> None:
54	    """The default diagnostic sink. stdout stays pipe-clean at all times."""
55	    print(f"logsift: {message}", file=sys.stderr)
56	
57	
58	def _normalize_dist(name: str) -> str:
59	    """Distribution names compare case-insensitively, with ``-``/``_`` alike."""
60	    return re.sub(r"[-_.]+", "-", name).lower()
61	
62	
63	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
64	class LoadedParser:
65	    """A validated parser together with the distribution that shipped it."""
66	
67	    parser: Parser
68	    dist: str
69	    name: str
70	
71	
72	class Registry:
73	    """The parsers loaded for one run, and the two ways of choosing among them."""
74	
75	    def __init__(
76	        self, parsers: Iterable[LoadedParser], *, warn: WarnFn = warn_stderr
77	    ) -> None:
78	        self._parsers = tuple(parsers)
79	        self._warn = warn
80	        self._collisions_warned: set[str] = set()
81	
82	    @property
83	    def parsers(self) -> tuple[LoadedParser, ...]:
84	        return self._parsers
85	
86	    def names(self) -> list[str]:
87	        """Every loaded parser name, sorted and deduplicated."""
88	        return sorted({entry.name for entry in self._parsers})
89	
90	    def resolve(self, spec: str) -> LoadedParser:
91	        """Look up ``NAME`` or ``DIST:NAME`` for ``--parser`` (SPEC 4.4)."""
92	        dist_spec, sep, name = spec.partition(":")
93	        if not sep:
94	            return self._resolve_bare(spec)
95	        wanted = _normalize_dist(dist_spec)
96	        for entry in self._parsers:
97	            if entry.name == name and _normalize_dist(entry.dist) == wanted:
98	                return entry
99	        raise UnknownParser(
100	            f"unknown parser {spec!r}: no installed distribution {dist_spec!r} "
101	            f"provides a parser named {name!r}. {self._available()}"
102	        )
103	
104	    def sniff_order(self) -> list[LoadedParser]:
105	        """Candidates for ``can_parse``, highest priority first (SPEC 5.1)."""
106	        order = sorted(
107	            self._parsers,
108	            key=lambda entry: (-entry.parser.priority, _normalize_dist(entry.dist)),
109	        )
110	        self._warn_collisions(order)
111	        return order
112	
113	    def _resolve_bare(self, name: str) -> LoadedParser:
114	        matches = [entry for entry in self._parsers if entry.name == name]
115	        if len(matches) == 1:
116	            return matches[0]
117	        if not matches:
118	            raise UnknownParser(f"unknown parser {name!r}. {self._available()}")
119	        providers = ", ".join(sorted(entry.dist for entry in matches))
120	        raise AmbiguousParser(
121	            f"parser name {name!r} is provided by more than one distribution: "
122	            f"{providers}. Disambiguate with --parser DIST:NAME."
123	        )
124	
125	    def _available(self) -> str:
126	        names = self.names()
127	        if not names:
128	            return "no parsers are installed"
129	        return f"installed parsers: {', '.join(names)}"
130	
131	    def _warn_collisions(self, order: Sequence[LoadedParser]) -> None:
132	        for name in self.names():
133	            if name in self._collisions_warned:
134	                continue
135	            sharing = [entry for entry in order if entry.name == name]
136	            if len(sharing) < 2:
137	                continue
138	            self._collisions_warned.add(name)
139	            candidates = ", ".join(
140	                f"{entry.dist} (priority {entry.parser.priority})" for entry in sharing
141	            )
142	            note = ""
143	            if sharing[0].parser.priority == sharing[1].parser.priority:
144	                note = (
145	                    ". Equal priorities were broken on distribution name, which is "
146	                    "deterministic but arbitrary"
147	                )
148	            self._warn(
149	                f"parser name {name!r} is provided by more than one distribution: "
150	                f"{candidates}; sniffing tries {sharing[0].dist} first{note}"
151	            )
152	
153	
154	def discover(*, warn: WarnFn = warn_stderr) -> Registry:
155	    """Load every parser published to ``logsift.parsers``.
156	
157	    A fresh registry each call, with no module-level cache, so a test that
158	    installs a distribution can rediscover it. Anything unloadable or
159	    non-conforming is skipped with a warning; discovery never raises.
160	    """
161	    loaded: list[LoadedParser] = []
162	    seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
163	    for entry_point in entry_points(group=ENTRY_POINT_GROUP):
164	        dist = _dist_name(entry_point)
165	        obj = _load(entry_point, dist, warn)
166	        if obj is None:
167	            continue
168	        parser = _validate(obj, entry_point, dist, warn)
169	        if parser is None:
170	            continue
171	        key = (_normalize_dist(dist), parser.name)
172	        if key in seen:
173	            warn(
174	                f"{dist} declares parser name {parser.name!r} more than once "
175	                f"(entry point {entry_point.name!r}); ignoring the duplicate"
176	            )
177	            continue
178	        seen.add(key)
179	        loaded.append(LoadedParser(parser=parser, dist=dist, name=parser.name))
180	    return Registry(loaded, warn=warn)
181	
182	
183	def _dist_name(entry_point: EntryPoint) -> str:
184	    dist = entry_point.dist
185	    if dist is None:  # pragma: no cover - metadata always carries a distribution
186	        return "<unknown distribution>"
187	    name: str | None = dist.metadata["Name"]
188	    return name or "<unnamed distribution>"
189	
190	
191	def _load(entry_point: EntryPoint, dist: str, warn: WarnFn) -> object | None:
192	    try:
193	        obj: object = entry_point.load()
194	    except Exception as exc:
195	        # Broad by design: a third party's import-time failure must not stop
196	        # the run, and any exception type is possible on the far side.
197	        warn(
198	            f"{dist}: could not load parser entry point {entry_point.name!r} "
199	            f"({entry_point.value}): {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}; skipping"
200	        )
201	        return None
202	    return obj
203	
204	
205	def _validate(
206	    obj: object, entry_point: EntryPoint, dist: str, warn: WarnFn
207	) -> Parser | None:
208	    """Inspect a loaded object without letting it abort discovery.
209	
210	    Reading an attribute runs plugin code whenever it is a property, so the
211	    inspection sits inside the same isolation boundary as loading it.
212	    """
213	    try:
214	        return _check_shape(obj, entry_point, dist, warn)
215	    except Exception as exc:
216	        warn(
217	            f"{dist}: parser entry point {entry_point.name!r} raised "
218	            f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc} while being inspected; skipping"
219	        )
220	        return None
221	
222	
223	def _check_shape(
224	    obj: object, entry_point: EntryPoint, dist: str, warn: WarnFn
225	) -> Parser | None:
226	    """Check the protocol by attribute, not by ``isinstance``.
227	
228	    Explicit checks name the attribute that is missing, and ``issubclass``
229	    against a data protocol is a ``TypeError`` waiting to happen.
230	    """
231	    missing = [attr for attr in _REQUIRED_ATTRS if not hasattr(obj, attr)]
232	    if missing:
233	        warn(
234	            f"{dist}: parser entry point {entry_point.name!r} is missing "
235	            f"{', '.join(missing)}; skipping"
236	        )
237	        return None
238	    # The attributes exist; from here the checks are on their values, which a
239	    # plugin can still get wrong in ways the static type does not describe.
240	    candidate = cast(Parser, obj)
241	    if candidate.api_version != API_VERSION:
242	        warn(
243	            f"{dist}: parser entry point {entry_point.name!r} declares api_version "
244	            f"{candidate.api_version!r}, but this logsift requires api_version "
245	            f"{API_VERSION}; skipping"
246	        )
247	        return None
248	    name = candidate.name
249	    if not isinstance(name, str) or not _NAME_RE.fullmatch(name):
250	        warn(
251	            f"{dist}: parser entry point {entry_point.name!r} declares an invalid "
252	            f"name {name!r}; names must match [a-z0-9_-]+; skipping"
253	        )
254	        return None
255	    priority = candidate.priority
256	    if not isinstance(priority, int):
257	        warn(
258	            f"{dist}: parser {name!r} declares a non-integer priority "
259	            f"{priority!r}; skipping"
260	        )
261	        return None
262	    columns = candidate.columns
263	    if isinstance(columns, str) or not _is_string_sequence(columns):
264	        warn(
265	            f"{dist}: parser {name!r} declares columns {columns!r}; columns must "
266	            f"be a sequence of column names, not a bare string; skipping"
267	        )
268	        return None
269	    return candidate
270	
271	
272	def _is_string_sequence(value: object) -> bool:
273	    return isinstance(value, Sequence) and all(isinstance(item, str) for item in value)
274

"""Shared fixtures.

``install_dist`` writes a real ``.dist-info`` directory onto ``sys.path`` so
that ``importlib.metadata.entry_points`` finds it exactly as it would find an
installed wheel. Nothing in the plugin tests monkeypatches discovery itself.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib
from collections.abc import Iterator, Mapping
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Protocol

import pytest

TESTS_DIR = Path(__file__).parent

METADATA = "Metadata-Version: 2.1\nName: {name}\nVersion: {version}\n"


class InstallDist(Protocol):
    """Publish ``entries`` as ``logsift.parsers`` entry points of ``dist``."""

    def __call__(
        self, dist: str, entries: Mapping[str, str], *, version: str = "1.0"
    ) -> Path: ...


@pytest.fixture
def install_dist(
    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> Iterator[InstallDist]:
    site = tmp_path / "site-packages"
    site.mkdir()
    # The fake parsers themselves live in the test tree, not in the fake site
    # directory; only their distribution metadata is synthesized.
    monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(TESTS_DIR))
    monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(site))

    def install(dist: str, entries: Mapping[str, str], *, version: str = "1.0") -> Path:
        info = site / f"{dist.replace('-', '_')}-{version}.dist-info"
        info.mkdir()
        (info / "METADATA").write_text(METADATA.format(name=dist, version=version))
        body = "\n".join(f"{name} = {value}" for name, value in entries.items())
        (info / "entry_points.txt").write_text(f"[logsift.parsers]\n{body}\n")
        importlib.invalidate_caches()
        return info

    yield install
    importlib.invalidate_caches()


@pytest.fixture
def warnings_seen() -> list[str]:
    """Collector passed to ``discover(warn=...)`` in place of stderr."""
    return []

"""The Common Log Format parser of SPEC section 11.1.

The parser is exercised as a plain object, the way SPEC 4.2 says a plugin may
be written, plus one test that it really is published to the entry point group.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import locale
from collections.abc import Iterator
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from logsift.parsers.clf import PARSER
from logsift.plugin import API_VERSION, Parser, discover
from logsift.record import ParseResult, Record

FIXTURE = Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures" / "access.log"

COMBINED = (
    '203.0.113.42 - - [01/Sep/2026:08:14:03 +0000] "GET /a HTTP/1.1" 200 12 '
    '"http://example.com/" "Mozilla/5.0"'
)


def fixture_lines() -> list[str]:
    """Every non-empty line of the fixture, newline stripped as SPEC 4.2 says."""
    return [line for line in FIXTURE.read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()]


def parse(line: str) -> ParseResult:
    result = PARSER.parse(line)
    assert result is not None, f"parser rejected {line!r}"
    return result


def records_for(lines: list[str]) -> list[Record]:
    """Build records the way SPEC 3 and 4.3 say the core will.

    ``pipeline`` does not exist yet, so this is the smallest stand-in for the
    one rule under test here: ``None`` from ``parse`` becomes a parse-error
    record, anything else does not.
    """
    records: list[Record] = []
    for lineno, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        result = PARSER.parse(line)
        if result is None:
            records.append(
                Record.parse_error_record(
                    raw=line,
                    source="access.log",
                    lineno=lineno,
                    reason="parser returned None",
                )
            )
            continue
        records.append(
            Record(
                raw=line,
                source="access.log",
                lineno=lineno,
                ts=result.ts,
                level=result.level,
                message=result.message,
                fields=result.fields,
                parse_error=False,
                parse_error_reason=None,
            )
        )
    return records


def test_the_fixture_has_the_lines_the_tests_assume() -> None:
    assert len(fixture_lines()) == 10


def test_it_satisfies_the_parser_protocol() -> None:
    assert isinstance(PARSER, Parser)
    assert PARSER.api_version == API_VERSION
    assert PARSER.name == "clf"
    assert PARSER.priority == 50
    assert list(PARSER.columns) == ["ts", "ip", "method", "path", "status", "bytes"]


def test_it_is_published_to_the_entry_point_group() -> None:
    # SPEC 4.1: the core reaches its own parsers only through discovery.
    entries = [e for e in discover().parsers if e.name == "clf"]
    assert [e.dist for e in entries] == ["logsift"]
    assert entries[0].parser is PARSER


def test_every_fixture_line_parses() -> None:
    for line in fixture_lines():
        assert PARSER.parse(line) is not None, line


def test_no_fixture_line_produces_a_parse_error() -> None:
    # The headline guarantee: the fixture is a clean file, so the records
    # SPEC 3 builds from these results carry no parse_error at all.
    records = records_for(fixture_lines())

    assert len(records) == 10
    offenders = [(r.lineno, r.parse_error_reason) for r in records if r.parse_error]
    assert offenders == []


def test_it_reads_the_first_fixture_line_field_by_field() -> None:
    result = parse(fixture_lines()[0])

    assert result.ts == datetime(2026, 9, 1, 8, 14, 3, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    assert result.level is None  # SPEC 11.1: CLF has no severity.
    assert result.message == "GET / HTTP/1.1"
    assert dict(result.fields) == {
        "ip": "203.0.113.42",
        "ident": None,
        "user": None,
        "method": "GET",
        "path": "/",
        "protocol": "HTTP/1.1",
        "status": 200,
        "bytes": 5123,
    }


def test_a_dash_ident_and_user_are_absent_not_the_string_dash() -> None:
    named = parse(fixture_lines()[2])

    assert named.fields["user"] == "alice"
    assert named.fields["ident"] is None


def test_a_dash_byte_count_is_none_rather_than_zero() -> None:
    # SPEC 11.1: `bytes` is int or None. A 304 sent no body; it did not send 0.
    result = parse(fixture_lines()[5])

    assert result.fields["status"] == 304
    assert result.fields["bytes"] is None


def test_the_query_string_stays_on_the_path() -> None:
    result = parse(fixture_lines()[3])

    assert result.fields["path"] == "/api/orders?page=2"
    assert result.message == "GET /api/orders?page=2 HTTP/1.1"


def test_it_reads_every_method_and_protocol_in_the_fixture() -> None:
    parsed = [parse(line) for line in fixture_lines()]

    assert {str(r.fields["method"]) for r in parsed} == {
        "GET",
        "POST",
        "DELETE",
        "HEAD",
    }
    assert {str(r.fields["protocol"]) for r in parsed} == {"HTTP/1.1", "HTTP/1.0"}
    assert [int(str(r.fields["status"])) for r in parsed] == [
        200,
        200,
        302,
        200,
        404,
        304,
        500,
        204,
        200,
        502,
    ]


def test_fixture_timestamps_are_utc_aware_and_ascending() -> None:
    stamps = [parse(line).ts for line in fixture_lines()]

    # SPEC 7: the parser hands over an aware datetime; normalizing to UTC is
    # the core's job, and these lines carry +0000 already.
    assert all(ts is not None and ts.utcoffset() == timedelta(0) for ts in stamps)
    assert stamps == sorted(stamps)  # type: ignore[type-var]


def test_a_non_utc_offset_is_converted_to_utc() -> None:
    result = parse('1.2.3.4 - - [10/Oct/2000:13:55:36 -0700] "GET /x HTTP/1.1" 200 2')

    assert result.ts == datetime(2000, 10, 10, 20, 55, 36, tzinfo=timezone.utc)


def test_a_half_hour_offset_is_kept_and_still_compares_as_utc() -> None:
    result = parse('1.2.3.4 - - [01/Sep/2026:12:00:00 +0530] "GET /x HTTP/1.1" 200 2')

    assert result.ts == datetime(2026, 9, 1, 6, 30, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    assert result.ts is not None
    assert result.ts.utcoffset() == timedelta(hours=5, minutes=30)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("abbreviation", "month"),
    [
        ("Jan", 1),
        ("Feb", 2),
        ("Mar", 3),
        ("Apr", 4),
        ("May", 5),
        ("Jun", 6),
        ("Jul", 7),
        ("Aug", 8),
        ("Sep", 9),
        ("Oct", 10),
        ("Nov", 11),
        ("Dec", 12),
    ],
)
def test_every_english_month_abbreviation_resolves(
    abbreviation: str, month: int
) -> None:
    line = f'1.2.3.4 - - [15/{abbreviation}/2026:00:00:00 +0000] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 1'

    result = parse(line)

    assert result.ts == datetime(2026, month, 15, tzinfo=timezone.utc)


def test_the_month_table_is_english_under_a_non_english_lc_time(
    non_english_lc_time: str,
) -> None:
    # SPEC 11.1: the locale trap. strptime("%b") would fail here.
    result = parse('1.2.3.4 - - [10/Oct/2000:13:55:36 +0000] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 1')

    assert result.ts == datetime(2000, 10, 10, 13, 55, 36, tzinfo=timezone.utc)


def test_a_localized_month_name_is_not_accepted() -> None:
    line = '1.2.3.4 - - [10/Okt/2000:13:55:36 +0000] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 1'

    assert PARSER.parse(line) is None


def test_combined_format_adds_referer_and_user_agent() -> None:
    result = parse(COMBINED)

    assert result.fields["referer"] == "http://example.com/"
    assert result.fields["user_agent"] == "Mozilla/5.0"


def test_common_format_omits_referer_and_user_agent_entirely() -> None:
    # SPEC 11.1 lists them as "when present"; SPEC 1 forbids inventing them.
    result = parse(fixture_lines()[0])

    assert "referer" not in result.fields
    assert "user_agent" not in result.fields


def test_a_dash_referer_is_absent_rather_than_the_string_dash() -> None:
    line = COMBINED.replace('"http://example.com/"', '"-"')

    result = parse(line)

    assert result.fields["referer"] is None
    assert result.fields["user_agent"] == "Mozilla/5.0"


def test_escaped_quotes_inside_the_user_agent_survive() -> None:
    line = COMBINED.replace('"Mozilla/5.0"', r'"Mozilla \"5.0\" \\ x"')

    result = parse(line)

    assert result.fields["user_agent"] == r'Mozilla "5.0" \ x'


def test_an_escaped_quote_in_the_request_does_not_end_it() -> None:
    line = '1.2.3.4 - - [01/Sep/2026:08:14:03 +0000] "GET /a\\"b HTTP/1.1" 200 1'

    result = parse(line)

    assert result.fields["path"] == '/a"b'
    assert result.message == 'GET /a"b HTTP/1.1'


def test_an_http_0_9_request_line_has_no_protocol() -> None:
    result = parse('1.2.3.4 - - [01/Sep/2026:08:14:03 +0000] "GET /old" 200 1')

    assert result.fields["method"] == "GET"
    assert result.fields["path"] == "/old"
    assert result.fields["protocol"] is None
    assert result.message == "GET /old"


def test_an_unsplittable_request_line_keeps_the_message_and_drops_the_parts() -> None:
    # nginx logs a bare "-" for a request it never read. The line is still a
    # well-formed CLF line, so it parses; the parts it cannot supply are None.
    result = parse('1.2.3.4 - - [01/Sep/2026:08:14:03 +0000] "-" 400 0')

    assert result.message == "-"
    assert result.fields["method"] is None
    assert result.fields["path"] is None
    assert result.fields["protocol"] is None
    assert result.fields["status"] == 400
    assert result.fields["bytes"] == 0


def test_a_request_line_with_extra_spaces_keeps_the_tail_on_the_path() -> None:
    result = parse('1.2.3.4 - - [01/Sep/2026:08:14:03 +0000] "GET /a b HTTP/1.1" 200 1')

    assert result.fields["method"] == "GET"
    assert result.fields["path"] == "/a b"
    assert result.fields["protocol"] == "HTTP/1.1"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("line", "why"),
    [
        ("", "empty"),
        ("   ", "blank"),
        ("not a log line at all", "no structure"),
        (
            '1.2.3.4 - - 01/Sep/2026:08:14:03 +0000 "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 1',
            "no brackets",
        ),
        ("1.2.3.4 - - [01/Sep/2026:08:14:03 +0000] GET / HTTP/1.1 200 1", "no quotes"),
        ('1.2.3.4 - - [01/Sep/2026:08:14:03 +0000] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200', "no bytes"),
        (
            '1.2.3.4 - - [01/Sep/2026:08:14:03 +0000] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 20 1',
            "short code",
        ),
        ('1.2.3.4 - - [01/Sep/2026:08:14:03 +0000] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 1.5', "float"),
        ('1.2.3.4 - - [01/Sep/2026:08:14:03] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 1', "no offset"),
        ('1.2.3.4 - - [32/Sep/2026:08:14:03 +0000] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 1', "day 32"),
        ('1.2.3.4 - - [01/Sep/2026:24:00:00 +0000] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 1', "hour 24"),
        ('1.2.3.4 - - [01/Sep/2026:08:14:03 +9900] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 1', "offset"),
        (
            '1.2.3.4 - - [01/Sep/2026:08:14:03 +0000] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 1 trailing',
            "junk",
        ),
        ('{"ts": "2026-09-01T08:14:03Z", "msg": "hi"}', "json line"),
        ("ts=2026-09-01T08:14:03Z level=info msg=hi", "logfmt line"),
    ],
)
def test_a_line_that_is_not_clf_is_declined(line: str, why: str) -> None:
    # SPEC 4.2: returning None means "not mine"; the core makes the record.
    assert PARSER.parse(line) is None, why


def test_can_parse_accepts_the_fixture() -> None:
    assert PARSER.can_parse(fixture_lines()) is True


def test_can_parse_accepts_a_bare_majority_and_rejects_a_bare_minority() -> None:
    good = fixture_lines()[:6]
    junk = ["nope"] * 5

    assert PARSER.can_parse(good + junk) is True
    assert PARSER.can_parse(good[:5] + junk + ["nope"]) is False


def test_can_parse_rejects_an_empty_or_blank_sample() -> None:
    assert PARSER.can_parse([]) is False
    assert PARSER.can_parse(["", "   "]) is False


def test_can_parse_rejects_other_formats() -> None:
    assert PARSER.can_parse(["ts=2026-09-01T08:14:03Z level=info msg=hi"] * 20) is False


def test_can_parse_does_not_raise_on_hostile_input() -> None:
    # SPEC 4.2: can_parse must be side-effect free and must not raise.
    assert PARSER.can_parse(["\x00�" * 100, "]" * 5000]) is False


def test_parsing_is_repeatable_and_holds_no_state() -> None:
    first = [parse(line) for line in fixture_lines()]
    second = [parse(line) for line in fixture_lines()]

    assert first == second


@pytest.fixture
def non_english_lc_time() -> Iterator[str]:
    """Switch LC_TIME to a non-English locale, skipping if none is installed."""
    for candidate in ("de_DE.UTF-8", "fr_FR.UTF-8", "de_DE", "fr_FR"):
        try:
            locale.setlocale(locale.LC_TIME, candidate)
        except locale.Error:
            continue
        try:
            yield candidate
        finally:
            locale.setlocale(locale.LC_TIME, "C")
        return
    pytest.skip("no non-English LC_TIME locale is installed")

"""The package skeleton: version, public surface, and module entry point."""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib
import re
from importlib.metadata import version as installed_version

import logsift


def test_version_is_a_release_string() -> None:
    assert re.fullmatch(r"\d+\.\d+\.\d+", logsift.__version__)


def test_the_installed_metadata_version_comes_from_the_package() -> None:
    # pyproject reads the version from logsift.__version__, so a drift here
    # means the two have been allowed to disagree.
    assert installed_version("logsift") == logsift.__version__


def test_the_public_surface_is_re_exported() -> None:
    assert logsift.Level is importlib.import_module("logsift.record").Level
    assert logsift.ParseResult is importlib.import_module("logsift.record").ParseResult
    assert logsift.Record is importlib.import_module("logsift.record").Record
    assert logsift.Parser is importlib.import_module("logsift.plugin").Parser
    assert logsift.API_VERSION == importlib.import_module("logsift.plugin").API_VERSION
    # SPEC 2.1 offers parse_iso8601 to plugin authors, so it is part of the
    # published surface, not an internal helper.
    assert (
        logsift.parse_iso8601
        is importlib.import_module("logsift.timeparse").parse_iso8601
    )


def test_python_dash_m_is_wired_to_the_console_script_target() -> None:
    main = importlib.import_module("logsift.cli").main
    assert importlib.import_module("logsift.__main__").main is main

"""The plugin contract of SPEC section 4: discovery, validation, resolution."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

import fake_parsers
from conftest import InstallDist
from logsift.plugin import (
    API_VERSION,
    AmbiguousParser,
    LoadedParser,
    Parser,
    Registry,
    UnknownParser,
    discover,
)


def loaded(registry: Registry, name: str) -> LoadedParser:
    matches = [entry for entry in registry.parsers if entry.name == name]
    assert len(matches) == 1, f"expected exactly one {name!r}, got {matches}"
    return matches[0]


def order_of(registry: Registry, names: set[str]) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Sniff order restricted to the parsers a test installed."""
    return [(e.name, e.dist) for e in registry.sniff_order() if e.name in names]


def test_api_version_is_one() -> None:
    assert API_VERSION == 1


def test_a_conforming_object_satisfies_the_runtime_protocol() -> None:
    assert isinstance(fake_parsers.SIMPLE, Parser)
    assert not isinstance(object(), Parser)


def test_discovery_reads_installed_distribution_metadata(
    install_dist: InstallDist, warnings_seen: list[str]
) -> None:
    install_dist("fake-simple", {"simple": "fake_parsers:SIMPLE"})

    entry = loaded(discover(warn=warnings_seen.append), "simple")

    assert entry.dist == "fake-simple"
    assert entry.parser is fake_parsers.SIMPLE
    assert warnings_seen == []


def test_the_parsers_own_name_wins_over_the_entry_point_name(
    install_dist: InstallDist, warnings_seen: list[str]
) -> None:
    # SPEC 4.2: `name` is the identifier for --parser, and it lives on the
    # parser, not in the installing project's pyproject.toml.
    install_dist("fake-simple", {"whatever": "fake_parsers:SIMPLE"})

    assert loaded(discover(warn=warnings_seen.append), "simple").dist == "fake-simple"


def test_discovery_is_not_cached_between_calls(
    install_dist: InstallDist, warnings_seen: list[str]
) -> None:
    install_dist("fake-simple", {"simple": "fake_parsers:SIMPLE"})
    first = discover(warn=warnings_seen.append)
    install_dist("fake-tie", {"tie": "fake_parsers:TIE"})
    second = discover(warn=warnings_seen.append)

    assert [e.name for e in first.parsers if e.name == "tie"] == []
    assert loaded(second, "tie").dist == "fake-tie"


def test_wrong_api_version_is_skipped_naming_both_versions(
    install_dist: InstallDist, warnings_seen: list[str]
) -> None:
    install_dist("fake-future", {"wrong-api": "fake_parsers:WRONG_API"})

    registry = discover(warn=warnings_seen.append)

    assert [e.name for e in registry.parsers if e.name == "wrong-api"] == []
    assert len(warnings_seen) == 1
    warning = warnings_seen[0]
    assert "fake-future" in warning
    assert str(API_VERSION + 1) in warning
    assert f"requires api_version {API_VERSION}" in warning

    assert "priority" in warnings_seen[0]
    assert "fake-partial" in warnings_seen[0]

1	"""Synthetic parsers that exercise the plugin contract (SPEC section 13).
2	
3	These objects are published as real entry points by the ``install_dist``
4	fixture, so discovery runs through ``importlib.metadata`` rather than a
5	monkeypatched shortcut. Annotating the well-behaved instances as ``Parser``
6	also makes ``mypy --strict`` check them against the published protocol.
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	from collections.abc import Sequence
12	from dataclasses import dataclass
13	from typing import Any
14	
15	from logsift.plugin import API_VERSION, Parser
16	from logsift.record import Level, ParseResult
17	
18	
19	@dataclass
20	class RecordingParser:
21	    """A well-behaved parser: every non-empty line becomes a message."""
22	
23	    api_version: int = API_VERSION
24	    name: str = "simple"
25	    priority: int = 10
26	    columns: Sequence[str] = ("ts", "message")
27	
28	    def can_parse(self, sample: Sequence[str]) -> bool:
29	        return bool(sample)
30	
31	    def parse(self, line: str) -> ParseResult | None:
32	        if not line:
33	            return None
34	        return ParseResult(ts=None, level=Level.INFO, message=line, fields={})
35	
36	
37	@dataclass
38	class AlwaysRaises(RecordingParser):
39	    """Raises on every line, so the circuit breaker of SPEC 4.3 fires."""
40	
41	    name: str = "always-raises"
42	
43	    def parse(self, line: str) -> ParseResult | None:
44	        raise RuntimeError("parser exploded")
45	
46	
47	@dataclass
48	class Intermittent(RecordingParser):
49	    """Raises only on lines carrying ``boom``; the run must still complete."""
50	
51	    name: str = "intermittent"
52	
53	    def parse(self, line: str) -> ParseResult | None:
54	        if "boom" in line:
55	            raise ValueError("bad line")
56	        return super().parse(line)
57	
58	
59	@dataclass
60	class CanParseRaises(RecordingParser):
61	    """Disqualifies itself for a source by raising from ``can_parse``."""
62	
63	    name: str = "bad-can-parse"
64	
65	    def can_parse(self, sample: Sequence[str]) -> bool:
66	        raise ValueError("sniff exploded")
67	
68	
69	@dataclass
70	class CollidingFields(RecordingParser):
71	    """Emits field names reserved by the core, per SPEC 4.5."""
72	
73	    name: str = "colliding-fields"
74	    columns: Sequence[str] = ("message", "lineno")
75	
76	    def parse(self, line: str) -> ParseResult | None:
77	        fields: dict[str, object] = {"message": "shadow", "lineno": -1, "app": "demo"}
78	        return ParseResult(ts=None, level=None, message=line, fields=fields)
79	
80	
81	@dataclass
82	class WrongApiVersion(RecordingParser):
83	    """Declares an api_version the core does not implement."""
84	
85	    api_version: int = API_VERSION + 1
86	    name: str = "wrong-api"
87	
88	
89	@dataclass
90	class MalformedName(RecordingParser):
91	    """Declares a name outside the documented ``[a-z0-9_-]+`` shape."""
92	
93	    name: str = "Bad Name!"
94	
95	
96	@dataclass
97	class BadPriority(RecordingParser):
98	    """Lies about ``priority``, which the core sorts sniff candidates by."""
99	
100	    name: str = "bad-priority"
101	    priority: Any = "high"
102	
103	
104	@dataclass
105	class StringColumns(RecordingParser):
106	    """Lies about ``columns``: a bare string iterates one column per character."""
107	
108	    name: str = "string-columns"
109	    columns: Any = "ts,message"
110	
111	
112	class MissingPriority:
113	    """Omits ``priority``, so validation must name the missing attribute."""
114	
115	    api_version = API_VERSION
116	    name = "missing-priority"
117	    columns: Sequence[str] = ("message",)
118	
119	    def can_parse(self, sample: Sequence[str]) -> bool:
120	        return True
121	
122	    def parse(self, line: str) -> ParseResult | None:
123	        return ParseResult(ts=None, level=None, message=line, fields={})
124	
125	
126	class ExplodingAttribute:
127	    """Raises from attribute access, so inspection itself has to be isolated."""
128	
129	    api_version = API_VERSION
130	    priority = 5
131	    columns: Sequence[str] = ("message",)
132	
133	    @property
134	    def name(self) -> str:
135	        raise RuntimeError("attribute exploded")
136	
137	    def can_parse(self, sample: Sequence[str]) -> bool:
138	        return True
139	
140	    def parse(self, line: str) -> ParseResult | None:
141	        return ParseResult(ts=None, level=None, message=line, fields={})
142	
143	
144	SIMPLE: Parser = RecordingParser()
145	ALWAYS_RAISES: Parser = AlwaysRaises()
146	INTERMITTENT: Parser = Intermittent()
147	CAN_PARSE_RAISES: Parser = CanParseRaises()
148	COLLIDING_FIELDS: Parser = CollidingFields()
149	WRONG_API: Parser = WrongApiVersion()
150	BAD_NAME: Parser = MalformedName()
151	BAD_PRIORITY: Parser = BadPriority()
152	STRING_COLUMNS: Parser = StringColumns()
153	MISSING_ATTRIBUTE = MissingPriority()
154	EXPLODING_ATTRIBUTE = ExplodingAttribute()
155	
156	# Two distributions publishing one name, at different priorities (SPEC 4.4).
157	DUP_HIGH: Parser = RecordingParser(name="dup", priority=60)
158	DUP_LOW: Parser = RecordingParser(name="dup", priority=40)
159

161	TIE: Parser = RecordingParser(name="tie", priority=25)

"""The key=value parser of SPEC section 11.2.

Exercised as a plain object, the way SPEC 4.2 says a plugin may be written.
The fixture is ``app.log``: eight key=value lines and two that no built-in

"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime, timezone

import pytest

# The two fixture lines that are not key=value at all: a Go panic and the
# stack line under it. SPEC 14 defers multiline records, so each is its own
# line, and neither built-in can make anything of either.
UNPARSEABLE_LINENOS = [5, 6]

def parse(line: str) -> ParseResult:
    result = PARSER.parse(line)
    assert result is not None, f"parser rejected {line!r}"
    return result


def fields_of(line: str) -> dict[str, object]:
    return dict(parse(line).fields)


def test_the_fixture_has_the_lines_the_tests_assume() -> None:
    assert len(fixture_lines()) == 10


def test_it_satisfies_the_parser_protocol() -> None:

"""Generic ``key=value`` lines, the format SPEC section 11.2 calls logfmt.

The parser is a module-level instance (``PARSER``), so the level table is
built once per process, as SPEC 4.1 requires of anything published to the
entry point group.

There is no regex here. logfmt's one hard rule is that a quoted value may
contain the separator, and a scanner that carries its position says that in a
way a pattern with a backtracking alternation only implies.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Iterator, Mapping, Sequence
from typing import Final, NamedTuple

from logsift.plugin import API_VERSION
from logsift.record import Level, ParseResult
from logsift.timeparse import parse_iso8601

# ASCII only: a non-breaking space inside a message is text, not a separator.
_SPACE: Final = " \t\r\n\v\f"
_QUOTE: Final = '"'
_EQUALS: Final = "="

# SPEC 11.2's core mapping. Matched exactly: logfmt keys are machine-written
# and lowercase by convention, and a `Level=` that stays in `fields` is
# visible in the output, while one silently folded into `level` is not.
_CORE_KEYS: Final[Mapping[str, str]] = {
    "ts": "ts",
    "time": "ts",
    "timestamp": "ts",
    "level": "level",
    "lvl": "level",
    "severity": "level",
    "msg": "message",
    "message": "message",
}

# The parser owns the translation; the core owns the ordering (SPEC 11.2).
# The digits are syslog severities 0-7. `notice` and 5 land on INFO because
# the core has no slot between INFO and WARN, and inventing one to hold them
# would change the meaning of every `level >= WARN` filter.
_LEVELS: Final[Mapping[str, Level]] = {
    "trace": Level.TRACE,
    "trc": Level.TRACE,
    "t": Level.TRACE,
    "debug": Level.DEBUG,
    "dbg": Level.DEBUG,
    "d": Level.DEBUG,
    "7": Level.DEBUG,
    "info": Level.INFO,
    "information": Level.INFO,
    "informational": Level.INFO,
    "notice": Level.INFO,
    "i": Level.INFO,
    "5": Level.INFO,
    "6": Level.INFO,
    "warn": Level.WARN,
    "warning": Level.WARN,
    "w": Level.WARN,
    "4": Level.WARN,
    "error": Level.ERROR,
    "err": Level.ERROR,
    "e": Level.ERROR,
    "3": Level.ERROR,
    "fatal": Level.FATAL,
    "critical": Level.FATAL,
    "crit": Level.FATAL,
    "panic": Level.FATAL,
    "emergency": Level.FATAL,
    "emerg": Level.FATAL,
    "alert": Level.FATAL,
    "f": Level.FATAL,
    "0": Level.FATAL,
    "1": Level.FATAL,
    "2": Level.FATAL,
}

# Go's logfmt writers quote with Go string syntax, so `\n` in a value is a
# newline rather than the letter n. Anything else after a backslash is the
# character itself, which covers `\"` and `\\` without a case for each. This
# is deliberately not shared with clf's unescaper: Apache escapes only the
# quote and the backslash, and reading `\n` as a newline there would corrupt
# a Windows user agent string.
_ESCAPES: Final[Mapping[str, str]] = {"n": "\n", "r": "\r", "t": "\t"}

_MIN_SNIFF_PAIRS: Final = 2


class _Token(NamedTuple):
    """One whitespace-delimited item. ``value`` is ``None`` for a bare key."""

    key: str
    value: str | None


def _scan(line: str) -> Iterator[_Token]:
    """Split a logfmt line into tokens. Total: every input yields something."""
    pos = 0
    end = len(line)
    while pos < end:
        if line[pos] in _SPACE:
            pos += 1
            continue
        start = pos
        while pos < end and line[pos] not in _SPACE and line[pos] != _EQUALS:
            pos += 1
        key = line[start:pos]
        if pos == end or line[pos] != _EQUALS:
            yield _Token(key, None)
            continue
        value, pos = _read_value(line, pos + 1)
        yield _Token(key, value)


def _read_value(line: str, pos: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """Read the value at ``pos``, returning it and the position after it."""
    if pos < len(line) and line[pos] == _QUOTE:
        return _read_quoted(line, pos + 1)
    start = pos
    while pos < len(line) and line[pos] not in _SPACE:
        pos += 1
    return line[start:pos], pos


def _read_quoted(line: str, pos: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """Read a quoted value, ``pos`` being just past the opening quote.

    An unterminated quote runs to the end of the line rather than
    disqualifying the line: the writer's newline is the only thing that was
    lost, and SPEC 1 would rather keep the text than drop it.
    """
    end = len(line)
    parts: list[str] = []
    while pos < end:
        char = line[pos]
        if char == _QUOTE:
            return "".join(parts), pos + 1
        if char == "\\" and pos + 1 < end:
            escaped = line[pos + 1]
            parts.append(_ESCAPES.get(escaped, escaped))
            pos += 2
            continue
        parts.append(char)
        pos += 1
    return "".join(parts), pos


def _count_pairs(line: str) -> int:
    return sum(1 for token in _scan(line) if token.value is not None and token.key)


class LogfmtParser:
    """The ``logfmt`` parser. Stateless, so one instance serves every source."""

    api_version: int = API_VERSION
    name: str = "logfmt"
    priority: int = 40
    columns: Sequence[str] = ("ts", "level", "message")

    def can_parse(self, sample: Sequence[str]) -> bool:
        """True when a majority of the sample carries two or more pairs.

        One pair is not enough to claim a source: a Common Log Format request
        line with a query string (``GET /orders?page=2``) already looks like
        one, and clf must keep its own files.
        """
        considered = 0
        matched = 0
        for line in sample:
            if not line.strip():
                continue
            considered += 1
            if _count_pairs(line) >= _MIN_SNIFF_PAIRS:
                matched += 1
        return considered > 0 and matched * 2 > considered

    def parse(self, line: str) -> ParseResult | None:
        core: dict[str, str] = {}
        fields: dict[str, object] = {}
        pairs = 0
        for key, value in _scan(line):
            if value is None:
                # A bare key is True by logfmt convention. One named for a
                # core field lands in `fields`, where SPEC 4.5's collision
                # warning will report it: `level` alone is not a severity.
                if key:
                    fields[key] = True
                continue
            if not key:
                # `=value` has no name a filter could ever reference, and a
                # key of "" in `fields` would be unaddressable dead weight.
                continue
            pairs += 1
            slot = _CORE_KEYS.get(key)
            if slot is None:
                fields[key] = value
            else:
                # Last write wins, which is what building a mapping does.
                core[slot] = value

        if pairs == 0:
            # Not a key=value line at all: a stack frame, a panic banner, or
            # prose. SPEC 4.2 says decline it and let the core record it.
            return None

        return ParseResult(
            ts=_read_ts(core, fields),
            level=_read_level(core, fields),
            message=core.get("message"),
            fields=fields,
        )


def _read_ts(core: Mapping[str, str], fields: dict[str, object]) -> datetime | None:
    """Read the timestamp value, preserving an unreadable one as ``ts_raw``."""
    text = core.get("ts")
    if text is None:
        return None
    ts = parse_iso8601(text)
    if ts is None:
        # SPEC 11.2. Assigned after the loop, so a log that ships its own
        # `ts_raw` key does not shadow the value the parser could not read.
        fields["ts_raw"] = text
    return ts


def _read_level(core: Mapping[str, str], fields: dict[str, object]) -> Level | None:
    """Translate the level value, preserving an unmapped one as ``raw_level``."""
    text = core.get("level")
    if text is None:
        return None
    level = _LEVELS.get(text.strip().lower())
    if level is None:
        fields["raw_level"] = text
    return level


PARSER: Final = LogfmtParser()

"""The key=value parser of SPEC section 11.2.

Exercised as a plain object, the way SPEC 4.2 says a plugin may be written.
The fixture is ``app.log``: eight key=value lines and two that no built-in
parser understands, which is the case SPEC 1 cares most about.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime, timezone

import pytest

from conftest import records_for
from conftest import fixture_lines as all_fixture_lines
from logsift.parsers import clf
from logsift.parsers.logfmt import PARSER
from logsift.plugin import API_VERSION, Parser
from logsift.record import Level, ParseResult

# The two fixture lines that are not key=value at all: a Go panic and the
# stack line under it. SPEC 14 defers multiline records, so each is its own
# line, and neither built-in can make anything of either.
UNPARSEABLE_LINENOS = [5, 6]


def fixture_lines() -> list[str]:
    return all_fixture_lines("app.log")


def parse(line: str) -> ParseResult:
    result = PARSER.parse(line)
    assert result is not None, f"parser rejected {line!r}"
    return result


def fields_of(line: str) -> dict[str, object]:
    return dict(parse(line).fields)


def test_the_fixture_has_the_lines_the_tests_assume() -> None:
    assert len(fixture_lines()) == 10


def test_it_satisfies_the_parser_protocol() -> None:
    assert isinstance(PARSER, Parser)
    assert PARSER.api_version == API_VERSION
    assert PARSER.name == "logfmt"
    assert PARSER.priority == 40
    assert list(PARSER.columns) == ["ts", "level", "message"]


def test_it_sniffs_after_clf() -> None:
    # SPEC 11: clf is the specific format and logfmt the generic one, so the
    # generic parser must not get first refusal on a Common Log Format file.
    assert PARSER.priority < clf.PARSER.priority


def test_eight_of_the_ten_fixture_lines_parse() -> None:
    parsed = [
        lineno for lineno, line in enumerate(fixture_lines(), 1) if PARSER.parse(line)
    ]

    assert parsed == [1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 9, 10]


def test_the_two_lines_no_parser_understands_become_parse_error_records() -> None:
    # SPEC 1: never lose a line. SPEC 3: a parse-error record carries the raw
    # text and nothing else, so nothing downstream reads an invented fact.
    records = records_for(PARSER, fixture_lines(), source="app.log")

    errors = [record for record in records if record.parse_error]
    assert [record.lineno for record in errors] == UNPARSEABLE_LINENOS
    assert [record.raw for record in errors] == [
        "panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference",
        "\tgoroutine 17 [running]:",
    ]
    for record in errors:
        assert record.parse_error_reason == "parser returned None"
        assert (record.ts, record.level, record.message) == (None, None, None)
        assert dict(record.fields) == {}
        assert record.source == "app.log"


def test_the_other_built_in_parser_declines_those_two_lines_as_well() -> None:
    # The claim above is "no parser can handle them", so it has to be checked
    # against every parser that ships, not only against the one under test.
    lines = fixture_lines()

    for lineno in UNPARSEABLE_LINENOS:
        assert clf.PARSER.parse(lines[lineno - 1]) is None


def test_the_eight_good_lines_produce_no_parse_error() -> None:
    records = records_for(PARSER, fixture_lines(), source="app.log")

    clean = [record for record in records if not record.parse_error]
    assert len(clean) == 8
    assert all(record.fields for record in clean)


def test_it_reads_the_first_fixture_line_field_by_field() -> None:
    result = parse(fixture_lines()[0])

    assert result.ts == datetime(2026, 9, 1, 8, 14, 3, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    assert result.level is Level.INFO
    assert result.message == "listening on :8080"
    assert dict(result.fields) == {"service": "api", "pid": "4131"}


def test_values_stay_strings_because_logfmt_carries_no_types() -> None:
    # SPEC 6.3 converts a numeric-looking string when the filter asks for a
    # number, so guessing int here would only add a way to guess wrong.
    assert fields_of(fixture_lines()[1])["duration_ms"] == "42"


def test_fractional_seconds_survive_to_microseconds() -> None:
    assert parse(fixture_lines()[1]).ts == datetime(
        2026, 9, 1, 8, 14, 7, 512000, tzinfo=timezone.utc
    )


def test_a_quoted_value_keeps_its_spaces_and_its_equals_signs() -> None:
    assert (
        fields_of(fixture_lines()[2])["query"]
        == "SELECT id FROM orders WHERE user_id = 91"
    )


def test_a_bare_key_is_true_per_the_logfmt_convention() -> None:
    assert fields_of(fixture_lines()[3])["retry"] is True


def test_an_escaped_quote_inside_a_value_survives() -> None:
    assert parse(fixture_lines()[8]).message == 'template "orders/show" not found'


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("line", "expected"),
    [
        ("ts=2026-09-01T08:14:03Z msg=hi", "ts"),
        ("time=2026-09-01T08:14:03Z msg=hi", "time"),
        ("timestamp=2026-09-01T08:14:03Z msg=hi", "timestamp"),
    ],
)
def test_every_timestamp_key_maps_to_the_core_field(line: str, expected: str) -> None:
    result = parse(line)

    assert result.ts == datetime(2026, 9, 1, 8, 14, 3, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    assert expected not in result.fields  # consumed, not duplicated


@pytest.mark.parametrize("key", ["level", "lvl", "severity"])
def test_every_level_key_maps_to_the_core_field(key: str) -> None:
    result = parse(f"{key}=warn msg=hi")

    assert result.level is Level.WARN
    assert key not in result.fields


@pytest.mark.parametrize("key", ["msg", "message"])
def test_every_message_key_maps_to_the_core_field(key: str) -> None:
    result = parse(f'{key}="disk full"')

    assert result.message == "disk full"
    assert key not in result.fields


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("text", "level"),
    [
        ("trace", Level.TRACE),
        ("TRACE", Level.TRACE),
        ("debug", Level.DEBUG),
        ("D", Level.DEBUG),
        ("info", Level.INFO),
        ("notice", Level.INFO),
        ("warn", Level.WARN),
        ("warning", Level.WARN),
        ("W", Level.WARN),
        ("err", Level.ERROR),
        ("error", Level.ERROR),
        ("E", Level.ERROR),
        ("crit", Level.FATAL),
        ("critical", Level.FATAL),
        ("fatal", Level.FATAL),
        ("panic", Level.FATAL),
    ],
)
def test_the_documented_level_aliases_map_case_insensitively(
    text: str, level: Level
) -> None:
    assert parse(f"level={text} msg=hi").level is level


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("digit", "level"),
    [
        ("0", Level.FATAL),
        ("1", Level.FATAL),
        ("2", Level.FATAL),
        ("3", Level.ERROR),
        ("4", Level.WARN),
        ("5", Level.INFO),
        ("6", Level.INFO),
        ("7", Level.DEBUG),
    ],
)
def test_every_syslog_severity_integer_maps(digit: str, level: Level) -> None:
    assert parse(f"level={digit} msg=hi").level is level


def test_the_fixture_uses_a_syslog_integer_and_an_uppercase_alias() -> None:
    assert parse(fixture_lines()[3]).level is Level.ERROR  # level=ERR
    assert parse(fixture_lines()[6]).level is Level.WARN  # lvl=4


def test_an_unmapped_level_is_kept_as_raw_level_and_never_guessed() -> None:
    # SPEC 11.2: the core owns the ordering, so a level it has no slot for
    # stays None rather than being rounded to the nearest severity.
    result = parse(fixture_lines()[7])

    assert result.level is None
    assert result.fields["raw_level"] == "silly"


def test_an_unparseable_timestamp_is_kept_as_ts_raw() -> None:
    # Epoch seconds are not ISO 8601, and inventing a reading of them would
    # be inventing a fact (SPEC 1).
    result = parse(fixture_lines()[8])

    assert result.ts is None
    assert result.fields["ts_raw"] == "1788250784"


def test_a_naive_timestamp_is_handed_over_naive() -> None:
    # SPEC 7: localizing with --assume-tz is the core's job, not the parser's.
    result = parse("ts=2026-09-01T08:15:12 msg=hi")

    assert result.ts == datetime(2026, 9, 1, 8, 15, 12)
    assert result.ts is not None and result.ts.tzinfo is None


def test_a_quoted_timestamp_may_use_a_space_separator() -> None:
    assert parse('ts="2026-09-01 08:15:12Z" msg=hi').ts == datetime(
        2026, 9, 1, 8, 15, 12, tzinfo=timezone.utc
    )


def test_an_unquoted_timestamp_cannot_carry_a_space() -> None:
    # The documented consequence of logfmt's own tokenization: the value ends
    # at the space, so the clock reads as a separate bare key.
    result = parse("ts=2026-09-01 08:15:12 msg=hi")

    assert result.ts == datetime(2026, 9, 1)
    assert result.fields["08:15:12"] is True


def test_an_empty_value_is_an_empty_string_not_a_missing_key() -> None:
    result = parse("msg= user=")

    assert result.message == ""
    assert result.fields["user"] == ""


def test_an_unterminated_quote_runs_to_the_end_of_the_line() -> None:
    assert parse('level=info msg="never closed').message == "never closed"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("escape", "expected"),
    [(r"\"", '"'), (r"\\", "\\"), (r"\n", "\n"), (r"\t", "\t"), (r"\q", "q")],
)
def test_backslash_escapes_inside_a_quoted_value(escape: str, expected: str) -> None:
    assert parse(f'msg="a{escape}b"').message == f"a{expected}b"


def test_a_repeated_key_takes_the_last_value() -> None:
    # A plain mapping is what a logfmt reader builds, and the last write wins
    # in one. Pinned because both halves of the run depend on it.
    result = parse("level=info level=error msg=first msg=second host=a host=b")

    assert result.level is Level.ERROR
    assert result.message == "second"
    assert result.fields["host"] == "b"


def test_a_core_key_repeated_under_two_aliases_takes_the_last_one() -> None:
    result = parse("ts=2026-09-01T00:00:00Z time=2026-09-02T00:00:00Z msg=hi")

    assert result.ts == datetime(2026, 9, 2, tzinfo=timezone.utc)


def test_a_key_with_no_name_is_dropped_rather_than_stored_unaddressable() -> None:
    # `=value` has no identifier a filter could ever name (SPEC 6.1).
    result = parse("=orphan msg=hi")

    assert "" not in result.fields
    assert result.message == "hi"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("line", "why"),
    [
        ("", "empty"),
        ("   ", "blank"),
        ("\tgoroutine 17 [running]:", "a stack frame"),
        ("panic: runtime error: nil pointer dereference", "a panic banner"),
        ("just some prose with no pairs at all", "prose"),
        ("Traceback (most recent call last):", "a python traceback header"),
        (
            '203.0.113.42 - - [01/Sep/2026:08:14:03 +0000] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 5123',

    ],
)
def test_a_line_with_no_key_value_pair_is_declined(line: str, why: str) -> None:
    # SPEC 4.2: returning None means "not mine"; the core makes the record.
    assert PARSER.parse(line) is None, why

"""The key=value parser of SPEC section 11.2.

Exercised as a plain object, the way SPEC 4.2 says a plugin may be written.
The fixture is ``app.log``: eight key=value lines and two that no built-in
parser understands, which is the case SPEC 1 cares most about.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime, timezone

import pytest

from conftest import records_for
from conftest import fixture_lines as all_fixture_lines
from logsift.parsers import clf
from logsift.parsers.logfmt import PARSER
from logsift.plugin import API_VERSION, Parser
from logsift.record import Level, ParseResult

# The two fixture lines that are not key=value at all: a Go panic and the
# stack line under it. SPEC 14 defers multiline records, so each is its own
# line, and neither built-in can make anything of either.
UNPARSEABLE_LINENOS = [5, 6]


def fixture_lines() -> list[str]:
    return all_fixture_lines("app.log")


def parse(line: str) -> ParseResult:
    result = PARSER.parse(line)
    assert result is not None, f"parser rejected {line!r}"
    return result


def fields_of(line: str) -> dict[str, object]:
    return dict(parse(line).fields)


def test_the_fixture_has_the_lines_the_tests_assume() -> None:
    assert len(fixture_lines()) == 10


def test_it_satisfies_the_parser_protocol() -> None:
    assert isinstance(PARSER, Parser)
    assert PARSER.api_version == API_VERSION
    assert PARSER.name == "logfmt"
    assert PARSER.priority == 40
    assert list(PARSER.columns) == ["ts", "level", "message"]


def test_it_sniffs_after_clf() -> None:
    # SPEC 11: clf is the specific format and logfmt the generic one, so the
    # generic parser must not get first refusal on a Common Log Format file.
    assert PARSER.priority < clf.PARSER.priority


def test_eight_of_the_ten_fixture_lines_parse() -> None:
    parsed = [
        lineno
        for lineno, line in enumerate(fixture_lines(), 1)
        if PARSER.parse(line) is not None
    ]

    assert parsed == [1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 9, 10]


def test_the_two_lines_no_parser_understands_become_parse_error_records() -> None:
    # SPEC 1: never lose a line. SPEC 3: a parse-error record carries the raw
    # text and nothing else, so nothing downstream reads an invented fact.
    records = records_for(PARSER, fixture_lines(), source="app.log")

    errors = [record for record in records if record.parse_error]
    assert [record.lineno for record in errors] == UNPARSEABLE_LINENOS
    assert [record.raw for record in errors] == [
        "panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference",
        "\tgoroutine 17 [running]:",
    ]
    for record in errors:
        assert record.parse_error_reason == "parser returned None"
        assert (record.ts, record.level, record.message) == (None, None, None)
        assert dict(record.fields) == {}
        assert record.source == "app.log"


def test_the_other_built_in_parser_declines_those_two_lines_as_well() -> None:
    # The claim above is "no parser can handle them", so it has to be checked
    # against every parser that ships, not only against the one under test.
    lines = fixture_lines()

    for lineno in UNPARSEABLE_LINENOS:
        assert clf.PARSER.parse(lines[lineno - 1]) is None


def test_the_eight_good_lines_produce_no_parse_error() -> None:
    records = records_for(PARSER, fixture_lines(), source="app.log")

    clean = [record for record in records if not record.parse_error]
    assert len(clean) == 8
    assert all(record.fields for record in clean)


def test_it_reads_the_first_fixture_line_field_by_field() -> None:
    result = parse(fixture_lines()[0])

    assert result.ts == datetime(2026, 9, 1, 8, 14, 3, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    assert result.level is Level.INFO
    assert result.message == "listening on :8080"
    assert dict(result.fields) == {"service": "api", "pid": "4131"}


def test_values_stay_strings_because_logfmt_carries_no_types() -> None:
    # SPEC 6.3 converts a numeric-looking string when the filter asks for a
    # number, so guessing int here would only add a way to guess wrong.
    assert fields_of(fixture_lines()[1])["duration_ms"] == "42"


def test_fractional_seconds_survive_to_microseconds() -> None:
    assert parse(fixture_lines()[1]).ts == datetime(
        2026, 9, 1, 8, 14, 7, 512000, tzinfo=timezone.utc
    )


def test_a_quoted_value_keeps_its_spaces_and_its_equals_signs() -> None:
    assert (
        fields_of(fixture_lines()[2])["query"]
        == "SELECT id FROM orders WHERE user_id = 91"
    )


def test_a_bare_key_is_true_per_the_logfmt_convention() -> None:
    assert fields_of(fixture_lines()[3])["retry"] is True


def test_an_escaped_quote_inside_a_value_survives() -> None:
    assert parse(fixture_lines()[8]).message == 'template "orders/show" not found'


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("line", "expected"),
    [
        ("ts=2026-09-01T08:14:03Z msg=hi", "ts"),

    assert key not in result.fields

"""Both built-in parsers reach the core through entry points (SPEC 4.1, 5).

The point of the plugin architecture is that logsift's own parsers are not
special. These tests read the installed distribution metadata, so they fail if
``pyproject.toml`` stops declaring a parser and they fail if the core starts
importing one directly.
"""

import subprocess
import sys

import pytest

from conftest import fixture_lines
from logsift.parsers import clf, logfmt
from logsift.plugin import LoadedParser, discover

BUILT_INS = {"clf": clf.PARSER, "logfmt": logfmt.PARSER}
